The  country  remained  as  a  net  importer  in  2024,  as  it  recorded  a  trade  in  energy
goods balance of 40.7 MTOE. This was 9.7 percent higher than its year-ago level and
attributed to a sharper rise in energy imports to 45.8 MTOE, which expanded by 9.1
percent or more than double the previous year’s 4.5 percent growth in energy exports
at 5.2 MTOE (Figure 16). Indonesia was the Philippines’ leading energy import partner
with 45.7 percent share to energy imports due to its dominant role as coal supplier for
power generation. This was followed by South Korea (10.6 percent), China (9.0 percent),
Saudi Arabia (7.1 percent), and Singapore (4.2 percent). Together, the top five trading
partners supplied 76.6 percent of the country’s total energy imports in 2024.
On the other hand, the Philippines shipped a total of 5.2 MTOE of combined oil, coal
and  condensate  volume  in  2024.  China  continued  to  be  the  primary  destination  of
Philippine  energy  commodities,  particularly  coal,  as  it  absorbed  4.0  MTOE  or  77.2
percent of total energy exports due to strong trade relations, cost-efficient logistics,
and  a  mutually  beneficial  trade  structure.  Other  key  export  markets  included  South
Korea  (7.4  percent),  Brunei  (4.2  percent),  Thailand  (2.5  percent),  and  Malaysia  (1.6
percent), bringing the top five destinations to a combined 92.8 percent share of total
exports.
